kjv: Who? where is he that hath taken venison
mine: Who then was it that hunted game
note: Hebrew mi-efo hu: efo is the particle "then, now"; the KJV reads it as ayeh/efoh "where", adding a second question.

kjv: thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven
mine: away from the fatness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and away from the dew of heaven
note: The preposition min in mishmanne ha-arets can be partitive ("of") as in v.28 or separative ("away from"). Esau's lament that no blessing remains (vv.36-38) and the harsh v.40 favour the separative sense; the KJV gives Esau the same blessing as Jacob.

kjv: when thou shalt have the dominion
note: The verb tarid (from rud, to roam or be restless) means breaking loose or growing restive; "have the dominion" follows an older derivation from radah (rule) and is not supported.
